question: im transferring from bergen community college with an associates in liberal arts, do i still have to do all the gen eds at ramapo or does the AA cover them?

body.answer:

Bergen is not named individually, but the pages apply to New Jersey community colleges [5, 6]. An A.A. is described as fully transferable as the first two years of a bachelor’s degree at New Jersey four-year institutions [14]. Ramapo’s catalog also says A.A. or A.S. students from a New Jersey community college should refer to its transfer-credit policy for more information [12].

Submit a final official transcript showing the conferred degree to receive the waiver [10]. Ramapo says A.A. or A.S. holders from a New Jersey community college have completed all general education requirements and do not need placement tests [9].

Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300 [6, 10].

Sources: [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/admitted-students/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [12](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1)

question: Do the transfer seminar or first year seminar requirements apply to me if I'm coming in as a junior?

First-Year Seminar is described as designed for first-time, full-time, first-year students [1], and is a general education requirement for first-year students to be taken in the fall of their first year [2]. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements under the stated policies [3]. Specifically, transfers without an A.A. or A.S. degree from a New Jersey community college who have at least 48 credits from an accredited institution are waived from First Year Seminar; during academic advisement, students are advised about applicable waivers and remaining requirements [4]. question: what are the gen ed requirements at ramapo? like how many credits are general education vs the major

body.answer:
Ramapo’s General Education curriculum is ten courses: four keystone courses (First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities); one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; and one course in two of the three distribution categories [10]. Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be completed within the first 64 credits. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major [10].

The curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits”; it is not stated as a fixed 41-credit requirement [6]. One course cannot satisfy two separate General Education competencies, and no more than two Gen Ed courses may also count toward your major [6]. For Fall 2026, the distribution category names differ between pages: section 9 says “Social Systems and Society,” while section 10 says “Systems, Sustainability, & Society” [9][10].

An undergraduate degree consists of General Education, a major, and free electives [12]. Ramapo requires 128 credits overall, but program requirements differ [13]. The pages don’t give a single credit total for your major or an exact Gen Ed-versus-major split; check your program with an adviser [13]. Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441.

Sources: [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [12](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/)

value.text: 1. Courses from an accredited college, university, or program with a grade of C (2.0) or better may be considered if they fit Ramapo’s curriculum. If a student wishes to have a particular course evaluated or counted, the student may contact the Convener of the appropriate program to review the course and its potential for transfer credit. If the Convener approves the transfer equivalency, this approval will be sent to the Office of Admissions, which will designate a person responsible for updating the appropriate systems. If the Vice Provost approves the transfer equivalency, this approval will be sent to the Office of Admissions, which will designate a person responsible for updating the appropriate systems. In some cases, it may be necessary to complete more than the minimum number of credits required for graduation from Ramapo College.

question: Should my kid major in nursing or biology if she wants to be a PA eventually? which one is better at ramapo

body.answer:
Ramapo’s pages do not say which major is better for becoming a PA or compare PA preparation, so I can’t recommend one based on verified college information. [1][3]

The Biology BS describes a flexible foundation in biology and lets students choose courses reflecting their interests. [1] The generic Nursing BSN is designed for students interested in becoming nurses; students complete general education and science courses before a two-year nursing sequence. [3] The pages describe Nursing preparation for nursing, not PA preparation. [3]

For help deciding, the Center for Student Success says to define the decision; gather information by reading the catalog, attending School events, asking questions and talking with advisors and students; use Cahill Career Development Center computer tests; consider PLACE, talk with upper-level students and professional advisors, and seek a related summer job; focus choices through classes and faculty conversations; then assess costs and risks, and gain co-op or internship experience. [11]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207. [11]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/)
